YouTube

Product Teardown · 2025

One platform.
Endless worlds.

YouTube has become a platform where almost anyone can find content relevant to their interests. Whether it is entertainment, learning a skill or solving a problem. The platform serves an incredibly diverse global audience, with millions of creators and billions of viewers.

How does YouTube keep creators creating, viewers watching, and advertisers spending, while the platform keeps growing?

PART 1

The Marketplace

Creators supply content. Viewers supply attention. Advertisers supply revenue. YouTube facilitates discovery and monetization. It sits in the middle, making sure the exchange keeps happening.

Stakeholder diagram

🎬
Creators

Give

  • Content
  • Expertise
  • Audience engagement

Get

  • Reach and audience
  • Revenue(platform ads, memberships, brand deals, Super Chat)
  • Recognition
YouTube

Give

  • Platform infrastructure
  • Content distribution
  • Recommendation engine
  • Discovery tools
  • Monetization tools

Get

  • Revenue (ads and Premium)
  • User behaviour and attention data
👁️
Viewers

Give

  • Attention and time
  • Money(Premium, memberships)
  • Engagement (likes, comments, shares)

Get

  • Entertainment
  • Knowledge and skill
  • Community
📣
Advertisers

Give

  • Money (advertising spend)
  • Marketing budget

Get

  • Audience attention
  • Brand awareness
  • Sales and conversions

Marketplace Flywheel

PART 2

The Attention Engine

The right content needs to reach the right person at the right time. Recommendation is the heart of this engine.

Why cracking attention matters

STEP 01
If users see relevant and interesting content, they watch, scroll and spend more time.
›
STEP 02
Once users come to relevant videos, relevant ads also can reach the right audience.
›
STEP 03
Advertisers happy, generates more revenue. Platform and creators happy, creates more. Users watch more.

How YouTube understands you — User Personas

📡
YouTube reads your signals
  • Watch history
  • Search history (recent weighs more than past)
  • Likes and dislikes
  • Subscriptions
  • Watch duration on each video
  • Recent interests (last few days matter most)

Among thousands of relevant videos — what gets recommended first?

YouTube looks at these six signals to decide priority.

01 Click-Through Rate (CTR)

Out of everyone who saw the thumbnail, how many actually clicked? High CTR means the title and thumbnail created curiosity.

I ate world's largest Pizza
8:03
10%
10 clicks out of 100 times shown
02 Average Watch Time

Average time a viewer spends on a video. A video with fewer views but high watch time beats a viral video nobody finishes.

A
1M views · 10 sec avg
= 8,000 mins total
B ✓
200K views · 15 min avg
= 500,000 mins total
03 Retention

How many viewers are still watching as the video goes on? It tells YouTube exactly where people lose interest and which videos hold people till the end.

Long Motivational Speech
Started: 50M
Ended: 2M ✗
Samay Raina — Still Alive
Started: 60M
Ended: 58M ✓
04 Total Watch Time

Total minutes watched across all viewers of a video. Not just views — how much real time did people give it?

100 views
drops to 80 viewers
by the end
500 views
drops to 10 viewers
by the end ✗
05 Session Time

The total time between when a user opens YouTube and when they close it. YouTube optimises for this above individual video metrics — a video that ends a session is penalised even if it is long.

POOR SESSION
Virat Kohli's best cover drives
5 min video
User watches, closes app
Session Time 5 min
GOOD SESSION
Virat's first century in England
7 min
↓
Top ten Virat's funny moments
5 min
↓
Virat and Anushka Interview
8 min
User keeps watching similar content
Session Time 20 min
06 Satisfaction (the hardest one)

Did the viewer actually enjoy it? This is the hardest signal to measure because it is not just one number. YouTube reads it through what users do after watching.

👍 Likes
👎 Dislikes
💬 Comments
🔗 Shares
🔔 Subscribes
🚫 "Not interested"
📋 Post-watch surveys

The Auction

Once a viewer clicks a video, there is an auction between all the advertisers who want to spend on that user. Whoever bids more, their advertisement gets broadcasted. An advertiser will have varied spend on different audiences.

👩 Sita watching CAT content
Interests: MBA, CAT Exam, Yoga, Health conscious
CAT Coaching High Bid
Lenovo Laptop Med Bid
Mamaearth Low Bid
👨 Arjun watching IPL
Interests: Cricket, Virat Kohli, Humor, Samay Raina
Sport Shoe High Bid
Amazon Prime Med Bid
Lenovo Laptop Low Bid
👩 Rajitha watching cooking
Interests: Cooking, Telugu Vlogs, Serials, Home Cleanliness
Aashirwad Masala High Bid
Mamaearth Med Bid
Surfexel Low Bid

Advertiser goal: ROAS

Advertisers give their whole budget to YouTube and track ROAS (Return on Ad Spend). Their goal is always Return > Spending.

₹15
Spent on ad
(Amazon Prime on a viewer)
→
₹300
Viewer converts
(buys the subscription)
=
20x
ROAS

How advertisers pay

CPM
Cost per Mille
For every 1,000 views of an ad, how much the advertiser pays.
CPC
Cost per Click
If the viewer clicks on the ad, the advertiser pays more.
CPA
Cost per Acquisition
If the viewer buys the product or converts, the advertiser pays the most.

YouTube Revenue Split

YouTube shares revenue with creators to encourage high-quality content which increases the ecosystem value.

🎬 Advertising
This is the largest income stream. YouTube shares 55% of net ad revenue with creators. For YouTube Shorts ads, creators receive 45%.
~$40B annually (2025)
⭐ YouTube Premium
YouTube distributes 55% of net Premium revenue to creators based on how much watch time their content gets from Premium users.
~$20B annually (2025)
💬 Memberships and Fan Funding
For direct community contributions such as monthly memberships, Super Chat, and Super Thanks, YouTube pays creators 70% of net revenues.
Creator revenue · Super Chat / Memberships

Creator Revenue Breakdown (RPM)

When creators track their individual earnings, they look at RPM — Revenue Per Mille, or earnings per 1,000 views. Their payouts are divided into three buckets on the analytics dashboard.

Ad Revenue
Paid per ad viewed.
Premium Revenue
Paid per minute watched by a Premium subscriber.
Memberships / Super Chats
Direct tipping and monthly subscription tiers from dedicated fans.

Monetization Engine

YouTube doesn't monetize videos.
It monetizes attention.
